title: Inspector Matadeen on the Moon and Other Satires

access.edition_or_version: Manas Books (Chennai), 1994; reissued Katha Press, 2003; 21 stories translated by C. M. Naim

mechanics.premise: Selected satirical stories in which ordinary, stolid characters are placed in bureaucratic, mystical, or supernatural situations that expose the absurdity of post-independence Indian institutions.
mechanics.point_of_view: A plain narrator who reports absurdity without surprise, holding a deadpan distance that never signals the reader where the joke sits.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Deadpan municipal register; mock-formal escalation of a single bureaucratic rule; understatement; the impossible treated as routine paperwork.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Normalcy -> literal pursuit -> absurd escalation -> dry, deflating punchline that returns to ordinary life.
mechanics.dialogue: Plain modern Hindi speech and institutional jargon, deployed sincerely by characters who never hear their own absurdity.
mechanics.conventions: Central to modern Hindi vyangya (satire); Parsai is credited with revolutionising Hindi satire by moving it from courtly targets to the bureaucratic maze.
tone_mechanisms: understatement in place of authorial sneer
irony whose judgement the reader supplies
mechanics.critical_reception: Parsai (1924-1995) won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1982 for Viklaang Shraddha ka Daur; his stories are widely taught and anthologised.
mechanics.verification_note: Existence, translator, editions, and author facts confirmed via Wikipedia API extract (Harishankar Parsai) on 2026-09-24 and library catalog metadata; technique characterized consistent with the repository's satirical-literature genre file. Analysis is partial and translation-mediated: assessed from Naim's English renderings and documented accounts, not from the Hindi originals; no passage reproduced.
